known_limitations: Free REST API blocks historical queries (HTTP 403). Requires approved academic research application. Empirical testing in V2.7 proved zero ground receivers within 50 km of DAM; sees en-route overflights only (>FL300).
Live-only point/radius API. No historical REST query endpoints for airport movements. Zero ground coverage at Damascus in V2.7 live tests.
Live open-data API only. No historical arrival/departure search. Sees high-altitude overflights (FL310+) in Levant, but no low-altitude terminal fixes at OSDI.
Public tracking map is live-only. Historical queries require commercial RapidAPI enterprise subscription. No free historical airport data downloads.
Provides open aeronautical metadata (runways, coordinates, frequencies, elevation) only. Does not record flight movements, schedules, or timestamps.
Free tier strictly limited to past 7 days of airport arrivals and departures. Raw downloads not provided. Older historical records require paid tier.
Free public interface limited to recent 2-3 days. Historical queries older than 7 days require paid AeroAPI tier ($100+/mo).
Live FIDS endpoint (flights.php) provides current flight schedule; retains ~10-15 days of recent past schedules but no multi-year historical archive. Lacks actual transponder/radar timestamps.
Publishes aggregate macro statistics (annual, semi-annual, monthly flight and passenger totals). Does not provide flight-level logs. Physical PDFs/gazettes must be acquired to elevate from Grade C.
Annual economic performance reviews summarize aggregate passenger and cargo volumes across Syrian transport infrastructure. Lacks individual flight events.

Reports official operational milestones (Dec 8 closure, Dec 18 domestic resumption, Jan 7 international resumption, Apr 8 reopening) and monthly aggregate traffic bulletins. Direct canonical permalinks currently unverified.

known_limitations: 578 daily rows in repo (289 arr, 289 dep) covering 2024-01-01 to 2024-10-15. Strictly scoped to DAM_ALP_LTK (composite 3-airport gateway). Disaggregation into Damascus-specific data is mathematically prohibited.

Contains periodic web snapshots of damairport.gov.sy, syrianair.com, chamwings.com, and flightradar24.com/data/airports/dam. Granularity depends on crawl frequency; provides timetable snapshots and archived news dispatches.

Business tier ($499/yr) offers up to 365 days of historical airport data. Multi-year raw CSV extracts require custom commercial sales quotation. Terrestrial receiver coverage in Syria is historically sparse; relies on MLAT and satellite ADS-B.

AeroAPI historical tier ($100–$1,000+/mo) or custom airport reports ($500–$3,000). Commercial license restricts redistribution or open publication. Radar coverage over Damascus is limited; relies on GDS schedule progress updates.

Provides raw aircraft state vectors via RapidAPI ($100–$1,000/mo). Does not parse airport arrivals/departures; requires custom trajectory modeling to infer touchdowns. Lacks low-altitude receiver coverage at OSDI.
Enterprise custom contract required ($10,000+/yr). Focuses on published airline schedules, capacity, and flight status. Does not provide cheap ad-hoc extracts. Highly restricted redistribution terms.

Enterprise contract required ($5,000–$20,000+/yr). Contains published airline schedules, equipment, and frequencies, not physical transponder sensor proofs. High cost barrier for independent research.
